proposal: The Mandate recommends reinstating the three 2018 Trump labor orders (EOs 13836, 13837, 13839) to renegotiate union contracts around management rights, curb official time for union activity, and limit grievances over removals and appraisals. It also calls for appointing the FLRA General Counsel and reactivating the Federal Service Impasses Panel, and suggests Congress consider whether public-sector unions are appropriate at all.

status_summary: The administration did not reinstate the 2018 orders by name; OPM said on 2025-02-07 that revoking Biden's EO 14003 did not by itself reinstate them. Instead EO 14251 (2025-03-27) and EO 14343 (2025-08-28) excluded dozens of agencies and subdivisions from the federal labor-relations statute on national security grounds, and an OPM memo of 2026-02-12 (revised 2026-02-17) told covered agencies to terminate their collective bargaining agreements, except for units protected by court orders, and to report monthly. The Ninth Circuit vacated the preliminary injunction in AFGE v. Trump on 2026-02-26, but injunctions remain for some units (for example DoD Education Activity and a VA master agreement), and the D.C. Circuit had not ruled as of late September 2026 on appeals argued 2025-12-15. On 2026-09-22 the FLRA dismissed a Defense Department case for lack of jurisdiction under the orders. FSIP members were appointed in July 2026 and an FLRA General Counsel was confirmed on 2026-08-07.

timeline.event: EO 14251 adds national security exclusions to the federal labor-management relations program for about 40 agencies and subdivisions; Sec. 6 requires reassignment of employees doing non-agency union business (official time) when a contract is terminated.
EO 14343 excludes additional agencies from the labor-relations program (for example the National Weather Service).

The House passes H.R. 2550, the Protect America's Workforce Act, 231 to 195 via discharge petition; it would restore bargaining rights removed by EO 14251 (vote count per AFL-CIO release). It has not passed the Senate in the sources reviewed.

OPM memo (revised 2026-02-17) tells agencies covered by EOs 14251 and 14343 to terminate or modify collective bargaining agreements, file monthly status reports, and not apply the guidance to units under a court order.
Ninth Circuit panel in AFGE v. Trump (No. 25-4014) vacates the preliminary injunction against EO 14251, reading the national security exemption broadly; merits remain pending.
timeline.source: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit

timeline.event: First Circuit declines to suspend a Rhode Island district court order requiring the VA to restore its master agreement with AFGE, while narrowing parts of the order (reported 2026-05-20).

Per a litigation tracker, unions file AFGE/NFFE v. DoD in D. Md. against a Defense Department memo of 2026-04-09 terminating collective bargaining agreements; a preliminary injunction motion followed on 2026-07-22 and none has been granted.
The President appoints eight members, including a chair, to the Federal Service Impasses Panel; they are sworn in between 2026-07-21 and 2026-07-27.
Charlton Allen is sworn in as FLRA General Counsel after Senate confirmation on 2026-08-07.
Per the same tracker (citing Government Executive), AFGE Council 238 sues in D. Mass. over EPA's termination of its union contract.

title: Limit federal employee unions: bargaining scope, official time, FLRA staffing
uncertainties: Official time: apart from EO 14251 Sec. 6, OPM's FY2025 official-time reporting call (due 2026-02-23) and the July 2026 OPM/MSPB proposed rule (which would bar official time to represent colleagues in covered proceedings), I found no standalone official-time order matching EO 13837; this was not searched exhaustively. On 2026-09-22 the FLRA voted 2-1 to dismiss a DoD case for lack of jurisdiction because DoD is covered by the orders (per Government Executive). I could not confirm the current status of the Rhode Island VA case after May 2026, or the number of contracts actually terminated. The share of the workforce affected is reported inconsistently across articles.
